model.equation:
SOC = clamp(SOC₀ − 100 I t / Q, 0, 100).
t_empty = Q SOC₀ / (100 I) for I > 0; t_empty = ∞ when I = 0.
I_eff = I while SOC > 0, otherwise 0; V = 320 + 0.8 SOC − I_eff R; P = V I_eff / 1000.
t_heat = min(t, t_empty); t_cool = max(0, t − t_empty).
T = Tₐ + I²R/8 · (1 − exp(−t_heat/0.8)) · exp(−t_cool/0.8).
assumptions: Illustrative 320–400 V pack with constant requested current until empty.
Current is zero after depletion; the lumped temperature then cools toward ambient with a 0.8-hour time constant.
A lumped thermal response and linear open-circuit voltage replace electrochemical dynamics.
No calibration, cell balancing, aging, or BMS safety logic.
Pack voltage, capacity, resistance, cooling, and current are invented; they do not describe the author’s hardware, publications, or test data.
The simple voltage relation omits RC polarization, EKF estimation, cell balancing, and converter dynamics.
Repository test counts and publication claims remain tied to their cited revisions; they are not inferred from this visual exercise.
model.introduction: The profile is a navigation and evidence document, not a native simulator. This added pack-level ohmic and SOC exercise is a starting question that points learners toward the appropriate source project.

modules.title: Turn a battery question into an evidence route
modules.objective: Use units and scope to select a relevant project from the profile.
steps: Read the Selected Engineering Work and validation-vocabulary sections.
Apply 100 Ah capacity, 12 A discharge, 90% initial SOC, and the reference resistance/ambient.
Predict remaining SOC after six hours, then identify which linked project would address richer electrical dynamics.

checkpoints.label: SOC falls to 18% after six hours
Terminal voltage under the declared ohmic relation

modules.reflection: Which evidence would distinguish this arithmetic check from a measured-cell validation claim?

modules.title: Find the energy-inventory boundary
modules.objective: Recognize that an apparently steady current request cannot continue after depletion.
steps: Double discharge current to 24 A with the same 100 Ah capacity and 90% starting SOC.
Predict depletion at 3.75 hours before running to six hours.
Use the profile to find the native continuity or energy-limit repository for a richer reserve calculation.

checkpoints.label: The modeled pack is empty at six hours
Delivered power is zero after depletion

modules.reflection: Why is an inventory boundary necessary even in a simple educational battery model?

modules.title: Separate scale from validation
modules.objective: Explain how a capacity change affects duration without validating a larger physical pack.
steps: Keep current at 24 A and double nominal capacity to 200 Ah.
Predict six-hour SOC and compare power and heating with the smaller-capacity case.
Read the profile’s thermal, BESS, and grid-service project descriptions to locate the next required evidence.

checkpoints.label: Larger capacity restores 18% SOC at six hours

modules.reflection: Which geometry, resistance, cooling, protection, and cell-matching assumptions would need reconsideration when scaling a real pack?

modules.title: Create an evidence-led project brief
modules.objective: Write a reproducible study question with a clear evidence tier and source of record.
steps: Use 100 Ah, 8 A, 70% initial SOC, 0.025 ohm resistance, and 25°C ambient.
Run and export the synthetic scenario with its parameters and limits.
Choose a linked native project and record the source revision, setup path, governing assumption, verification plan, and missing measurement evidence.

checkpoints.label: Synthetic delivered power at six hours

modules.reflection: How would you label a result that is unit-tested and reproducible but not independently replicated or physically validated?

source.scope: This browser lab is a standalone teaching approximation. Use the linked source for the project implementation.
